actions.broad_permissions.name: Workflow permissions are least-privilege
actions.broad_permissions.description: Every workflow declares the permissions its token gets.
actions.broad_permissions.recommendation:
Declare the minimum at the top of each workflow, and widen it only on the job that needs more:
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write  # only where it is actually used

actions.cloud_oidc.name: Cloud deploys use short-lived credentials (OIDC)
actions.cloud_oidc.description: Cloud access from workflows uses OpenID Connect instead of a stored key.

actions.pinned_sha.name: GitHub Actions pinned to a commit SHA
actions.pinned_sha.description: Every third-party action is pinned to a commit SHA.
actions.pinned_sha.recommendation:
Reference actions by full commit SHA:
  uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683  # v4.2.2
Tools such as pin-github-action or Dependabot can do this and keep it updated.

actions.pull_request_target.name: No unsafe pull_request_target workflow
actions.pull_request_target.description: No pull_request_target or workflow_run workflow checks out pull request code.

actions.script_injection.name: No script injection in workflows
actions.script_injection.description: No workflow pastes an issue, pull request, comment or branch name into a script.

actions.self_hosted_public.name: No self-hosted runners in a public repository
actions.self_hosted_public.description: No self-hosted runner can be started by someone outside the repository.

ai.agent_ci_exposed.name: AI agents in CI cannot be steered by outsiders
ai.agent_ci_exposed.description: Every AI agent in CI either runs on events only collaborators can cause, checks who triggered it, or cannot write.

ai.instructions_clean.name: Agent instruction files hold no secrets or internal addresses
ai.instructions_clean.description: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and similar files contain no credentials or internal hostnames.

ai.mcp_pinned.name: MCP servers run a pinned version
ai.mcp_pinned.description: Every locally started MCP server names an exact version.

ai.mcp_secrets.name: No credentials in MCP server configs
ai.mcp_secrets.description: MCP configs reference credentials from the environment instead of containing them.

ci.branch_protection.name: Default branch is protected
ci.branch_protection.description: Branch protection stops anyone pushing straight to main without review.

ci.linter.name: Linter or formatter configured
ci.linter.description: A single enforced code style removes a whole class of review comments.
ci.linter.recommendation: Add a linter config: ruff.toml or pyproject.toml for Python, eslint.config.js for JavaScript, .golangci.yml for Go.

ci.pipeline.name: CI/CD pipeline configured
ci.pipeline.recommendation: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml (or .gitlab-ci.yml) that runs your tests and linter on every push.

ci.security_scan.name: Security scanning in the pipeline
ci.security_scan.description: A scanner in CI catches vulnerable dependencies and leaked secrets before they merge.
ci.security_scan.recommendation: Add a scanning step to CI. Free options: Trivy for images and dependencies, gitleaks for secrets, CodeQL for code. Each is a single job in your existing workflow.

ci.tests.name: Tests run in CI
ci.tests.description: Running the test suite on every commit is what stops a regression from reaching production.
ci.tests.recommendation: Add a test step to the pipeline (pytest, jest, go test — whatever your stack uses).

deps.cve.name: Known vulnerabilities in dependencies
deps.cve.description: Checked 2 dependencies against OSV.dev — no known vulnerabilities.

deps.lockfile.name: Lock file present
deps.lockfile.description: A lock file pins exact versions so the build you tested is the build you ship.
deps.lockfile.recommendation: Generate a lock file: `pip freeze > requirements.lock`, `npm install`, `poetry lock`, `go mod tidy` or `cargo build` depending on your stack.

deps.manifest.name: Dependency manifest present
deps.manifest.description: Without a manifest the environment cannot be reproduced or scanned for vulnerabilities.
deps.manifest.recommendation: Add a dependency file: requirements.txt or pyproject.toml (Python), package.json (Node), go.mod (Go), Cargo.toml (Rust).

deps.pinned.name: Dependencies pinned to exact versions
deps.pinned.description: Ranges such as >= mean two builds of the same commit can install different code.

docker.dockerfile.name: Dockerfile present
docker.dockerfile.description: A Dockerfile gives everyone — and production — the same reproducible runtime.
docker.dockerfile.recommendation: Add a Dockerfile at the repository root. Use a multi-stage build to keep the final image small.

docker.dockerignore.name: .dockerignore configured
docker.dockerignore.description: .dockerignore keeps .git, node_modules and secrets out of the build context.

docker.healthcheck.name: Healthcheck defined
docker.healthcheck.description: Without a healthcheck the orchestrator cannot tell a starting container from a broken one.
docker.healthcheck.recommendation:
Add to docker-compose.yml:
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/health/"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 3

docker.multistage.name: Dockerfile uses a multi-stage build
docker.multistage.description: A multi-stage build leaves compilers and build tools out of the shipped image.
docker.multistage.recommendation:
Split the build:
FROM python:3.11 AS builder
RUN pip install --prefix=/install -r requirements.txt
FROM python:3.11-slim
COPY --from=builder /install /usr/local

docker.nonroot.name: Container runs as a non-root user
docker.nonroot.description: A container running as root turns a process escape into host access.
docker.nonroot.recommendation:
Add to the Dockerfile:
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
USER app

docker.pinned_base.name: Base image is pinned (not :latest)
docker.pinned_base.description: Base images are pinned to explicit tags.
docker.pinned_base.recommendation: Replace floating tags with explicit ones, for example FROM python:3.11-slim or FROM node:20-alpine. Pin by digest for the strongest guarantee.

docker.resource_limits.name: Resource limits set in compose
docker.resource_limits.description: Without memory limits one runaway container can take the whole host down with it.
docker.resource_limits.recommendation:
Add to each service:
deploy:
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512M
      cpus: "0.5"

docs.changelog.name: CHANGELOG maintained
docs.changelog.description: A changelog tells users and your own team what actually changed between releases.
docs.changelog.recommendation: Add CHANGELOG.md and follow the keepachangelog.com format.

docs.contributing.name: CONTRIBUTING guide
docs.contributing.description: A contribution guide lowers the barrier for the next person who wants to help.
docs.contributing.recommendation: Add CONTRIBUTING.md describing the flow: fork, branch, pull request, review.

docs.readme.name: README exists
docs.readme.description: The README is the first thing anyone opening the repository reads.
docs.readme.recommendation: Add README.md covering what the project does, how to run it locally, and how to run the tests.

docs.readme_quality.name: README explains how to run the project
docs.readme_quality.description: A README without setup instructions costs every new developer their first day.
docs.readme_quality.recommendation: Expand the README with a Getting started section: prerequisites, install command, how to run the app, how to run the tests.

docs.templates.name: Pull request / issue templates
docs.templates.description: Templates make sure every PR and bug report arrives with the context reviewers need.

gitlab_ci.cloud_oidc.name: Cloud deploys use short-lived credentials (OIDC)
gitlab_ci.cloud_oidc.description: Cloud access from the pipeline uses OpenID Connect instead of a stored key.

gitlab_ci.pinned_images.name: GitLab CI images are pinned
gitlab_ci.pinned_images.description: Every job image and service names a tag or a digest.
gitlab_ci.pinned_images.recommendation:
Name an exact version, or better a digest:
  image: python:3.12.7-slim
  image: python@sha256:<digest>   # cannot be repointed
Renovate can keep either up to date.

gitlab_ci.pinned_includes.name: GitLab CI includes are pinned
gitlab_ci.pinned_includes.description: Every included pipeline file is local, a GitLab template, or pinned to a version.

iac.no_hardcoded_credentials.name: No provider credentials hardcoded in Terraform
iac.no_hardcoded_credentials.description: Credentials come from variables or the environment.

iac.open_ingress.name: No sensitive ports open to the internet
iac.open_ingress.description: No sensitive port is reachable from 0.0.0.0/0.

iac.remote_state.name: Terraform state is remote and locked
iac.remote_state.description: Local state means no team can apply safely — two people applying at once corrupt it, and the file usually holds secrets in plain text.

iac.scanning.name: Terraform is scanned in CI
iac.scanning.description: An IaC scanner catches a misconfigured resource in review, not after it is live.
iac.scanning.recommendation:
Add Checkov or tfsec to the pipeline:
- run: pip install checkov && checkov -d . --quiet --compact

ops.activity.name: Repository is actively maintained
ops.activity.recommendation: Either bring the project up to date or archive it so nobody depends on it by mistake.

ops.env_example.name: .env.example documents required variables
ops.env_example.description: When .env is ignored and undocumented, nobody new can start the project.
ops.env_example.recommendation: Add .env.example listing every variable the app reads, with placeholder values.

ops.gitignore.name: .gitignore configured
ops.gitignore.description: Without .gitignore, build output and local secrets end up committed sooner or later.
ops.gitignore.recommendation: Add a .gitignore for your stack — gitignore.io generates one from a language list.

ops.license.name: License specified
ops.license.description: Without a license, nobody else has legal permission to use the code.
ops.license.recommendation: Add a LICENSE file — MIT or Apache 2.0 for open source, or a proprietary notice for closed code.

ops.observability.name: Observability tooling is wired in
ops.observability.recommendation:
Add the three signals:
• Errors:  sentry-sdk
• Metrics: prometheus-client plus a /metrics endpoint
• Traces:  opentelemetry-sdk
• Logs:    structlog or loguru for structured JSON output

security.codeowners.name: CODEOWNERS is configured
security.codeowners.description: CODEOWNERS automatically requests review from the right people on security-critical paths.

security.dependency_updates.name: Automated dependency updates
security.dependency_updates.description: Dependabot or Renovate opens pull requests as soon as a security patch is released.
security.dependency_updates.recommendation: Add .github/dependabot.yml so security patches arrive as pull requests instead of waiting for someone to notice them.

security.env_gitignored.name: .env is ignored by git
security.env_gitignored.description: This project does not use a .env file.
security.env_gitignored.recommendation: Add a `.env` line to .gitignore, then confirm the file is not already tracked with `git ls-files .env`. If it is, remove it from history and rotate every value in it.

security.env_not_committed.name: .env file is not committed
security.env_not_committed.description: No .env file is tracked in the repository.
security.env_not_committed.recommendation: Delete the file from the repository (`git rm --cached .env`), rotate every value it contained, and add `.env` to .gitignore.

security.no_secrets.name: No secrets committed to the repository
security.no_secrets.description: No credentials found in the repository source.
security.no_secrets.recommendation:
Treat every value found as compromised and rotate it now — removing the line is not enough, it stays in git history.
1. Rotate the credential at the provider.
2. Move it to an environment variable or a secret manager.
3. Purge it from history with git-filter-repo or BFG.
4. Add a pre-commit hook (gitleaks or detect-secrets) so the next one never lands.

security.security_policy.name: Security policy (SECURITY.md)
security.security_policy.description: Tells researchers how to report a vulnerability privately instead of opening a public issue.
security.security_policy.recommendation: Add SECURITY.md with a contact address and your expected response time.
